subject: Post-call: EdgeCraft comparison — lab scope & latency/throughput asks
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgecraft.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2023 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: EdgeCraft comparison — lab scope & latency/throughput asks

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Call highlights:
- EdgeCraft is doing an internal comparison between your current hyperscaler setup (HyperscaleX) and Redwood’s hosted inference for a set of user-facing prompts (chat + summarization).
- Your primary concern is p95/p99 latency for short interaction flows and steady-state tokens/sec during bulk scoring.
- You want objective A/B data so your infra team can sign off.

Proposed lab scope (what Redwood will run):
1) Short prompt latency A/B: 1k concurrent users simulated, typical payload = 80–140 tokens, measure p50/p95/p99 and first-byte latency.
2) Microburst scenario: 2000 qps spike for 30s, measure tail behavior and error rate.
3) Bulk throughput: 8K long sequences (512–1k tokens) to measure tokens/sec sustained for 10m windows.
4) Cache/kv-warmup sensitivity: measure cold vs warm KV cache for common prefixes.

Asks from EdgeCraft (what we need from you):
- A test endpoint (staging creds) and a sample traffic trace (1–2k requests) to replay (anonymized).
- Expected distributions: typical tokens per request, percent long-form, and any synthetic payloads you want included.
- Any constraints (eg: max seq length, auth headers).

Attachments: edgebench-plan.xlsx (detailed run matrix), run_instructions.md (how we’ll execute).

Timeline: If you can share creds by end of day Thursday (7/27), we can run an initial pass next week and share a readout within 3 business days.

Next steps / owners:
- Samir: provide creds + sample trace.
- Marcus: set up Redwood run harness and baseline.
- Jordan: define pass/fail thresholds with EdgeCraft product lead.

Thanks — I’ll stand up the run doc and invite the infra folks once we have creds.

Best,
Stephanie
Principal SDR, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

----
Attachments:
- edgebench-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet: test matrix, sequences, concurrency targets)
- run_instructions.md (markdown: harness commands, environment vars)

From: Samir Patel <samir@edgecraft.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeCraft Platform Team <platform@edgecraft.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2023 18:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: EdgeCraft comparison — lab scope & latency/throughput asks

Thanks, Stephanie — appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick answers: 

- We can stand up a staging token for you (staging-key-red-ec) and a replay trace (sanitized) — I’ll send both by EOD Thursday.
- Typical distribution: 70% short (avg 120 tokens), 25% medium (300–600 tokens), 5% long (>800 tokens). Peak concurrently is variable but we saw 1.2k active users during last campaign; microbursts occur during daily syncs.
- Target thresholds from our PM: p95 < 120ms for short prompts; p99 < 250ms is ideal but negotiable if throughput is much better.

One ask on our side: please include HyperscaleX as the comparison target (they’ve given us baseline numbers but we want a side-by-side repeatable test). Also curious about any differences in tail behavior when you use prefix/KV caching vs disabled — we suspected caching hides occasional microburst penalties.

I’ll upload the trace and creds to the Drive link you shared and ping when done.

—Samir
Lead Platform Engineer, EdgeCraft
samir@edgecraft.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2023 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: EdgeCraft comparison — lab scope & latency/throughput asks

Looping in to prioritize the test matrix and owners. Draft matrix below — please comment if any item should be deprioritized: 

Priority 1 (must-run)
- Short prompt A/B (p50/p95/p99) @ typical concurrency (1k) — steady-state 10m windows
- Microburst stress: 30s spikes to 2k qps — measure tail and error contribution

Priority 2
- Bulk scoring throughput (tokens/sec) for long sequences, sustained 10m windows
- Cold vs warm KV cache: same workload before/after prefix warmup

Measurement notes (team):
- Use consistent measurement harness for both Redwood and HyperscaleX — same client, same replay trace, same inter-arrival times.
- Measure CPU/GPU utilization and request queueing (queue depth) to explain tail events.
- Capture first-byte and last-byte timings, and tokens/sec as a derived metric (tokens / total_time).

Owners: Marcus (lab run + instrumentation), Lauren (data validation + graphs), Jordan (pass/fail criteria), Stephanie (Customer comms).

Marcus — can you draft a short runbook with command lines we can hand to Samir’s infra team (ssh/endpoint details redacted) and an estimate for total GPU hours?

Jordan
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2023 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: EdgeCraft comparison — lab scope & latency/throughput asks

Thanks — attaching an initial runbook and the baseline CSV. High level plan + commands below (I’ll drop the full run_instructions.md into the Drive folder):

Test scaffolding:
- Harness: ghz-style HTTP load generator (internal wrapper) with deterministic inter-arrival based on provided trace.
- Warmup: 5m warmup at 50% load before each measured window to stabilize KV caches and queues.
- Measurement window: 10m per phase; report p50/p95/p99; sample per-second token counts.

Key commands (example):

# set env
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=staging-key-red-ec
export TARGET_URL=https://staging.edgecraft.ai/v1/generate

# run single-phase: 1000 concurrent clients, 10m window
./run-harness --clients 1000 --duration 600 --trace replay.json --out results_short_1000.json

Notes on cache effects:
- We’ll run each short-prompt phase twice: first run with prefix-caching disabled, then with caching enabled and a 5m prefix warmup. Compare p95 delta and tokens/sec.
- For microbursts, we’ll increase clients quickly to replicate instantaneous arrival patterns rather than ramping.

GPU hours estimate: ~12 GPU-hours for full matrix (short + microburst + throughput) on our medium nodes. If EdgeCraft prefers faster turnaround we can parallelize but will need temporary extra capacity.

Attachments: run_instructions.md, p95-baseline.csv (sample baseline from HyperscaleX provided by Samir).

Marcus
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir@edgecraft.ai>

All good on our side — I uploaded the sanitized trace and staging_key to the Drive link and invited the three redwood emails to the folder. I also left a short note in the HubSpot deal with an expected decision window (2–3 weeks).

Proposed lab window: Mon 31 Jul — Wed 2 Aug. We’ll have two infra engineers on standby for any access issues. Please confirm run times and whether you need any additional headers or signing.

Also: we’d like the readout to include a simple summary slide with the following: p95 delta (Redwood vs HyperscaleX), tokens/sec comparison, and one sentence on root cause for any >20% delta in tail. That will help our execs sign off quickly.

Thanks — looking forward.

Samir
Lead Platform Engineer, EdgeCraft
samir@edgecraft.ai
